_comment: Known, accepted disagreements between the machine-generated contract oracle (*.contract.json) and this repo's TypeScript surface. tests/oracle-freshness.test.ts fails on any drift that is NOT listed here, and equally fails on a listed entry that no longer drifts, so these lists can only shrink. Adding an entry is a deliberate, reviewable act: it records debt, it does not excuse it. Regenerate the oracle first (pnpm oracle:refresh) before touching this file.

_keys.stale_routes: Route a registered MCP tool points at, which the live backend no longer serves. The coverage gate fails on every one of these; listing it here only records that we know, it does not silence that gate. Burn down by retiring or repointing the tool, then deleting the entry.
_keys.uncovered_routes: Public /api route the backend serves with an #[ApiMethod] operation, which no MCP tool covers. ratchet.json caps how many there may be per service; this list says which ones they are.
_keys.hidden_surfaces: Route-prefix -> reason. A DELIBERATELY UNPUBLISHED surface: routes under the prefix are served to a gated caller population and must NEVER get MCP tools, openapi:public entries or docs pages. Both gates subtract these prefixes from the public MCP surface before measuring coverage, and oracle-freshness fails on a listed prefix the backend no longer serves, so the list cannot rot. This is not debt (uncovered_routes is debt); it is a standing decision, recorded here so the next docs sweep does not helpfully document a hidden surface.

linkedin._note: Both lists are empty: this service is at FULL MCP coverage. stale_routes is empty because no registered tool points at a route this backend has dropped. The 23 entries that used to sit there (linkedin-searches / -search-results / -tracked-posts / -comments / -engagements, absorbed by the §9.6 linkedin-scraping + data-requests surface) are gone because the tools that pointed at them were retired or repointed; the webhooks + webhook_logs tools moved to mcp.orchestration and now point at gtm.service.orchestration, which serves them. uncovered_routes was the 13 linkedin-auto-scrape* routes, and they came off on 2026-07-27 with mcp.linkedin/linkedin_auto_scrapes (10), linkedin_auto_scrape_runs (2) and linkedin_auto_scrape_results (1). The 3 linkedin-posting routes (create-post, comment, react) were covered earlier by mcp.linkedin/linkedin_posting.

hidden_surfaces.api/infra-pool/: partner-plane pool mirror of the two §9.6 surfaces (research data_requests.md §Infra pool; gs.gtm-integration CONTRACT §3.2), restored 2026-08-31. Gated by InfraPoolSurface to plan=partner (fail-closed 404) and HIDDEN BY DESIGN: no MCP tool, no openapi:public entry, no docs page, ever.

orchestration._note: Both lists are empty: this service is at FULL MCP coverage. stale_routes has been empty since the webhook surface (10 routes) moved here from gtm.service.linkedin. uncovered_routes was the 11 mass-actions / mass-action-items routes; the 2 child ones (search, retry) came off on 2026-07-27 with mcp.orchestration/mass_action_items, and the 9 parent ones came off the same day with mcp.orchestration/mass_actions (search, get, create, delete, preview, metrics, pause, resume, release). The 8 api/example-entity routes that used to sit here are gone for good: the service.empty ExampleEntity bundle was deleted from gtm.service.orchestration on 2026-07-26 (backend routes, entity folder, tests, table), so they were never a product surface and are no longer served.

id._note: Both lists are empty: this service is at FULL MCP coverage again. uncovered_routes held the nine public email-boxes routes (search, create, confirm-checkout, update, preview-resize, resize, delete, move-in, retry) from 2026-11-12, when they landed with decision D12 of product/decision_records/001_email_box_per_workspace.md (a workspace may own several email servers) ahead of their tools, until mcp.id/email_boxes covered all nine the same day: seven served on /mcp/id/billing (create, resize and delete behind the preview gate, resize's first call quoting through preview-resize) and two REST only (surface api, a line in the REST reference and no tool): preview-resize, now the first call of resize_email_box, and confirm-checkout, which follows a person's own gesture in the app (paying in the Paddle checkout only the app can open). A tenth route, preview-create, joined on 2026-11-16 with its definition in the same change (REST only, the first call of create_email_box, which had no quote until then). confirm-checkout is not a hidden_surfaces entry: the route is public to every caller with can_manage_billing and a REST integrator running its own checkout needs it, while hidden_surfaces is for a surface served to a gated caller population. Before that, uncovered_routes held the 5 account-shares routes until 2026-07-27, when mcp.id/account_shares covered them and the baseline went 5 -> 0. The account-transfers routes are deliberately absent from this list and always were: they carry no #[ApiMethod], so they are not an MCP surface at all (share = MCP, transfer = no MCP, by design).

email._note: Empty since 2026-11-13: @gtm/mcp-email covers every public route of gtm.service.email (65), so nothing is uncovered and nothing is stale. Until that day uncovered_routes listed the entire public surface route by route (65 on 2026-11-12, from 44 on 2026-07-27), because the service had no MCP package at all and a service missing from the freshness gate's list is not covered debt, it is invisible debt. A route the backend adds from here on fails the gate until a tool covers it or it is listed here with its reason.
